messages:
anya: heads-up, saw a weird memory growth on one tenant serving lots of very long chats. looks like KV residency keeps creeping every 6-8 minutes :confused:
kevin_r: same node or across nodes?
anya: same node pool, pod restart reduces memory but it climbs back. pprof heap shows a lot of small pinned pages that never get evicted.
todd: do we have a snapshot? any flamegraphs or pprof output?
anya: pasted the short dump from last run:
```
pprof heap (30s sample)
- total resident: 48.2GB
- kv_pages_pinned: 13,412
- avg_kv_page_size: 4KB
- top refs by tenant: tenant-42 (6.8k), tenant-8 (3.1k), tenant-3 (1.2k)
- page_fragmentation_ratio: 1.28
```
maria: tenant-42 is a noisy RLHF test team, they do longctx>32k often. maybe longctx growth + fragmentation means pages not reusable.
kevin_r: curious if batching heuristic is inflating kv usage — we recently changed batch coalescing to prefer longer sequences for throughput. that could keep larger KV caches around per-request.
anya: yeah, the timing correlates with the new batch window tweak rolled last week.
todd: can we repro in staging? schedule a load run with long sessions from tenant-42 workload generator. I can run a variant with old batch settings and new.
anya: started a short run against staging-3. attaching pprof after 15m.
runtime-bot: load-test started by todd on staging-3 (id: lt-2418).
anya: interesting diff: when we force smaller batches, pinned pages drop by ~40% and fragmentation ratio goes down to 1.05.
kevin_r: that suggests batching heuristic prolongs per-req KV residency. two knobs: (1) decrease coalescing bias for long sequences, (2) add aggressive LK (last-k) eviction window for tenants exceeding longctx quota.
maria: eviction window would help but could hurt tail latency for those tenants. prefer per-tenant quota + soft decay first.
todd: we also saw pprof symbols referencing the fallback kernel path (no AVX512) on some of the hosts handling tenant-42 — could be slower kernels holding locks longer.
anya: good catch — host image mismatch meant some nodes used fallback matmul kernels with higher CPU time per token. increased CPU + long batches => slower KV turnover.
kevin_r: plan: 1) roll back batch coalescing change on a small ring for affected pool, 2) add a short-lived sampler to detect tenants with KV residency delta > threshold, 3) add a per-tenant decay that reduces kept prefix TTL when flagged.
maria: also add a flag to the routing policy to avoid sending known longctx tenants to fallback-kernel hosts. routing change is cheap and reversible.
todd: I'll run an A/B on staging: baseline vs rollback vs rollback+decay. will collect pprof and eviction traces.
anya: quick workaround deployed: pin tenant-42 to a smaller batch window and to AVX nodes. after 10m, pinned pages dropped from 6.8k -> 2.1k.
kevin_r: can we improve observability? add a per-tenant kv_residency gauge, plus incremental page-fingerprint logs (digest of pages and age buckets). keep them low-cardinality.
anya: sketch for page fingerprint log:
```
KV_PAGE_FINGERPRINT tenant=tenant-42 bins=[0-30s:120,30-300s:480,300-1800s:320,>1800s:60] pinned=6800 frag_ratio=1.27
```
maria: that should let us detect drift quickly. also add a rolling median for refdist so we know reuse patterns.
kevin_r: long term: consider per-tenant slab isolator to avoid fragmentation from noisy tenants — either soft quotas by slab class or slab segregation. both have tradeoffs.
todd: can we simulate fragmentation? I have a microbench that churns different page sizes and simulates slot reuse. will run with the current runtime kernel and fallback kernel to see sensitivity.
anya: noted two follow-ups: (A) ops: route longctx tenants away from fallback-kernel hosts; (B) infra/engineers: run staged A/B on batch coalescing knob + add residency gauge and fingerprint logs.
maria: i'll add the routing flag and the observability tickets. will also draft an emergency runbook: if a tenant's pinned pages > X and frag_ratio > 1.2 -> throttle batch coalescing and migrate.
kevin_r: add a small safety: if eviction rate drops below expected and memory growth continues, auto-fallback to per-request uncoalesced path for that tenant.
anya: sounds good. thx team. let's reconvene after todd's A/B in ~45m. :thumbsup:
devex-bot: todd's load-test completed. results uploaded to /s3/lt-2418/results.
todd: uploaded pprof tarballs and the fragmentation sim results to the folder. early look: fallback-kernel hosts consistently show ~1.6x higher pinned time and higher fragmentation. i'll post graphs in 15m.
anya: awesome. next sync after graphs.
maria: filed tickets: RNF-1123 (residency gauge + fingerprint), RNF-1124 (routing flag), RNF-1125 (per-tenant decay policy + runbook).
kevin_r: added a doc note about kernel parity to infra checklist — don't let mixed-kernel hosts serve the same tenant pools.
anya: ok closing this thread for now, will open follow-up with A/B graphs.
